chunks.text: 80-year-old male, Retired, resident of Ang Mo Kio, Singapore.
Left wrist fracture, healed without issues in 2010
Completed course of antibiotics for UTI in 2015

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Liew, the anesthesiologist. I'll be speaking with you today about your upcoming surgery. Can you tell me a bit about why you're having this TURP done?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah, yes doctor. My prostate been swollen for a while, causing trouble urinating. Sometimes I can't go at all, very uncomfortable. Urologist said TURP is the best option lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I see. Let's go over your medical history. Can you list all your current medications for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. I take amlodipine 10mg every day for blood pressure, lisinopril 20mg also daily. Metformin 500mg twice a day for diabetes, atorvastatin 20mg at night for cholesterol, and aspirin 75mg daily. Oh, and omeprazole 20mg, but I stopped that two weeks ago as instructed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Do you have any known allergies, Mr. Tan? The records say 'no known allergies,' but I'd like to confirm directly.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Allergies? Hmm... I think I had a reaction once to penicillin when I was younger. Got a rash all over, very itchy. But that's all, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Ah, that's important. Was it specifically penicillin, or other antibiotics too?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Only penicillin, doctor. My skin turned red and itchy like a heat rash. Never had issues with other antibiotics.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Noted. Let's move to your health conditions. You have hypertension, diabetes, high cholesterol, and stage 2 kidney disease. Are these well-controlled?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, my BP usually around 130/80, sugars okay with metformin. Cholesterol under control with statin. Kidneys stable, no recent issues.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Have you eaten or drunk anything this morning? Remember, nothing after midnight except clear fluids up to 2 hours ago.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. Only sipped some water this morning, stopped by 6am. Followed the instructions strictly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Have you had anesthesia before? Any reactions or complications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, once for cataract surgery. They gave spinal anesthesia then too, no problems at all. Woke up fine.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Lastly, how's your overall energy and mobility? Can you walk comfortably, climb stairs?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Still walking daily, but slower now. Prostate issues make it hard sometimes, but I manage stairs with rest stops.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Tan. We'll proceed with spinal anesthesia plus local infiltration as planned. No contraindications noted. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. All clear. Thank you for explaining everything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] Spinal anesthetic performed with bupivacaine twenty-five milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] Local infiltration with lidocaine twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] Midazolam two milligrams IV for sedation

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:07] Fentanyl fifty micrograms IV administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] Airway maintained spontaneously, no intubation required

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] Peripheral IV line established in left antecubital vein

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] Crystalloid fluid bolus five hundred milliliters given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:25] Blood pressure drop to seventy over forty, treated with phenylephrine ten micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:30] Heart rate increased to one hundred twenty, atropine point five milligrams given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Mr. Tan, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm okay, Doctor. Got some pain here and there, but not too bad lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Can you rate your pain on a scale from 0 to 10 for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe 4 or 5? It's manageable, but I feel some discomfort when moving.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or feeling like you want to vomit? Sometimes spinal anesthesia can cause that.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A bit queasy earlier, but settled down after they gave me something. No vomiting, thank God.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Breathing comfortable? Any shortness of breath or airway issues?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing's fine. Throat a bit sore from the tube, but I can talk okay.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Do you remember anything during the surgery? Sometimes patients recall bits.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Not much, Doctor. Felt some pressure here and there, heard voices, then woke up here.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Your blood pressure's stable, but we're watching your diabetes and kidney function. Any concerns?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, worried about sugar levels, but nurse said it's under control. Urine output's a bit less, but no swelling.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: We'll keep monitoring. Stay hydrated and follow your meds. Any other issues?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, all good. Thank you, Doctor. I'll rest and drink more water.

Intraoperative management included bupivacaine 25mg, midazolam 2mg, and fentanyl 50mcg. Airway maintained spontaneously without intubation. Peripheral IV in left antecubital vein. Crystalloid bolus of 500ml administered.
Blood pressure dropped to 70/40 at 08:25, prompting phenylephrine administration. Heart rate increased to 120 at 08:30, treated with atropine 0.5mg.

Anticipated issues include hypotension (spinal anesthesia and antihypertensives), tachycardia/arrhythmias (hemodynamic instability), PONV (opioid/benzodiazepine), glycemic challenges (fasting/diabetes), renal monitoring (CKD and fluid/BP changes), airway compromise (elderly with spinal), analgesia needs (post-TURP), bleeding risk (aspirin), and delirium (benzodiazepine in elderly).

Monitor for hypotension and tachycardia; assess glycemic control; monitor renal function; evaluate airway patency; manage analgesia needs; watch for bleeding; assess for delirium; consider antiemetics for PONV risk.
